publications.title: ESMA publishes latest edition of its newsletter
publications.summary: ESMA publishes latest edition of its newsletter 29 October 2026 ESMA newsletter The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has published today the latest edition of its Spotlight on Markets newsletter , covering key activities and publications from September and October 2026. This edition opens with the appointment of Carlo Comporti as ESMA’s next Chair . His appointment was confirmed by the Council of the European Union, and he will take up his position on 1 November 2026. Top news highlights include ESMA’s 2027 Annual Work Programme , setting out priorities for stronger, simpler and more integrated EU capital markets; the new Union Strategic Supervisory Priority on digital innovation; and the European Supervisory Authorities’ priorities for 2027 . publications.title: ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting
publications.summary: ESMA proposes simpler EU Taxonomy reporting 29 October 2026 Issuer disclosure Sustainable finance The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, has published its Final Report providing technical advice to the European Commission on simplifying key performance indicators under the Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act. ESMA recommends narrowing the mandatory operating expenditure (OpEx) KPI to non-capitalised research and development expenditure. It also proposes simpler group Taxonomy reporting, including removing the weighted-average KPI, and targeted measures to make disclosures more proportionate, clearer and easier to use. The Technical Advice was coordinated with the other European Supervisory Authorities, in particular on the voluntary use of counterparties’ OpEx information and group-level Taxonomy reporting. publications.title: FCA encourages former Verus Financial Services Limited customers to check if they can claim with FSCS
publications.summary: Compensation may be available to former Verus customers through the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS), subject to assessment. If you were a customer of Verus Financial Services Limited, you can now check to see if you can claim for compensation on the FSCS website. The FCA is supporting the FSCS as it assesses claims against Verus Financial Services Limited and decides whether individual claims are eligible for compensation.Verus was an independent financial adviser firm providing investment, pension, mortgage, equity release and insurance advice.Since 2025, the firm does not have the permission to carry out any regulated financial services activity in the UK, including providing any financial advice. They also cannot sell, transfer or reduce their asset without the FCA’s approval.Read about the FCA’s action taken against Verus Financial Services Limited.

publications.title: What does 'fair value' look like in practice? Three years into the Consumer Duty, here’s what we’ve learned.
publications.summary: Fair value is a simple yet important principle at the heart of the Consumer Duty: the price customers pay should be reasonable, relative to the benefits they get. But applying that principle in practice requires judgement.Three years into the Consumer Duty, we’re seeing clear differences between firms that have embedded fair value into their approach and those that still need to strengthen their assessments, evidence and monitoring.We recently reviewed how firms across the consumer finance market assess, evidence and monitor fair value. We also carried out focused work on fees and charges across a range of credit products, and supervisory work on consumer hire and third-party ownership agreements for home energy infrastructure.Many firms are getting it right, building fair value into how they design, price and monitor their products. publications.title: FCA stops HTX's crypto promotions
publications.summary: The FCA has secured High Court undertakings to ensure that HTX (formerly Huobi), a global crypto exchange, will not knowingly promote cryptoasset services unlawfully to UK consumers. The FCA took legal action against HTX in October 2025 for breaking UK financial promotion rules. HTX had failed repeatedly to engage with the FCA. Following the commencement of proceedings, HTX took steps to exit the UK. The FCA and Huobi Global S.A. have now reached a settlement in the case. HTX is no longer active in the UK. Consumers can no longer make deposits, and new UK users cannot sign up to the platform.
